audit_scope.description: This batch covers EL precompile execution (EVMC precompile flow via EIP-2003, identity precompile, ECRECOVER signature recovery, ModExp gas repricing via EIP-2565), EVM comparison instructions (Cancun LT/GT/EQ/SLT/SGT/ISZERO), EL state management and access list processing (Amsterdam fork), CL weak subjectivity checkpoint validation and long-range attack protection, CL beacon metrics monitoring (PeerDAS data columns, consensus state, network health), and Fusaka/Osaka network upgrade activation (EIP-7607 fork scheduling and BPO blob parameter forks). EIP-7329 governance routing is informational only.

in_scope: Gas Cost Calculation (ModExp repricing, comparison gas)
State Management and Access List Processing (Amsterdam)

el_attack_vectors.threat: Submit transactions with crafted precompile inputs (malformed ECRECOVER signatures, oversized ModExp inputs for gas exhaustion, identity precompile data amplification)
Eclipse attacks, send invalid blocks with malformed state transitions, propagate blocks with incorrect access list processing

cl_attack_vectors.threat: Propose invalid blocks, submit conflicting attestations, attempt long-range attacks with historical validator keys

cl_attack_vectors.entry_point: External APIs (checkpoint sync endpoint, MEV-Boost relay)
cl_attack_vectors.threat: Provide incorrect weak subjectivity checkpoints to direct nodes to attacker-controlled fork, serve invalid data column sidecars

misclassified_entities.reason: The Ethereum client is the system under audit, not an external entity. It is the host calling the EVMC module internally.
Beacon state is internal CL state data used for computation, not an external entity sending data into the system.
Client implementation teams are governance actors operating outside runtime protocol boundaries; not a runtime data source.
Network operators are governance/operational actors; their runtime interaction is via CLI (captured by EXT-NODE-OPERATOR) not a separate entity.
Core developers are governance actors who define fork rules offline; they do not send runtime data into the protocol.
EIP authors are governance participants; they do not interact with the runtime protocol as external data sources.
Proposal authors interact with the EIP governance process, not the runtime Ethereum protocol. EIP-7329 is informational.
Documentation users accessing EIP/ERC websites are not interacting with the Ethereum protocol runtime.

trusted_external_entities.name: User via JSON-RPC (Transaction Submission)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any user or DApp can submit transactions via public JSON-RPC. Transactions may contain crafted precompile inputs (ECRECOVER, ModExp, identity) or malformed access lists. No authentication required.

trusted_external_entities.name: Calling Contract via EVM CALL to Precompile
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: EVM CALL/STATICCALL/DELEGATECALL to precompile addresses (0x01 ECRECOVER, 0x04 Identity, 0x05 ModExp)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any contract can invoke precompiles with arbitrary calldata. Input data is fully untrusted and may attempt signature malleability (ECRECOVER), gas exhaustion (ModExp with large inputs), or data amplification (identity). Consolidates EXT-CALLER, EXT-UNTRUSTED-CALLER, EXT-CALLER-CONTRACT, EXT-CONTRACT-CALLER.

trusted_external_entities.name: DoS Attacker via ModExp Spam
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Attacker may attempt to submit many cheap ModExp calls to exhaust node resources. EIP-2565 mitigates with minimum gas floor of 200 and repriced gas formula, but the attack vector remains relevant.

trusted_external_entities.name: Network Peer via P2P (Block Propagation)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Peer nodes propagate blocks over unauthenticated P2P network. Blocks may contain invalid structure, incorrect state transitions, or malformed access lists. Full validation required.

trusted_external_entities.name: Node Operator via CLI (WS Checkpoint)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Node operator provides weak subjectivity checkpoint at startup. Authenticated via local CLI access (physical/SSH), but the checkpoint content itself must be validated against the canonical chain. If the operator provides a checkpoint from an attacker fork, the node will follow the wrong chain.

trusted_external_entities.name: Long-Range Attacker via P2P (Conflicting Fork)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Adversary controlling historical validator private keys may attempt to create a conflicting finalized chain. Weak subjectivity mechanism and slashing conditions protect against this, but the attack vector is fundamental to PoS security.

trusted_external_entities.name: Network Peer via P2P (Data Column Sidecars)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Peers propagate data column sidecars over unauthenticated gossipsub. Each sidecar requires KZG batch verification and inclusion proof verification before acceptance. Invalid data could cause reconstruction failures or consensus divergence.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Transaction Pool (access list processing, Amsterdam fork)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Full transaction validation required including access list structure, gas pricing for warm/cold slots, and intrinsic gas calculation. Malformed access lists must be rejected.
Identity precompile performs no input validation by design—gas cost must scale with input size to prevent resource amplification. Output is untrusted pass-through data.

Input signature parameters (v, r, s) must be validated: v must be 27 or 28, r and s must be in range (0, SECP256K1N). Invalid inputs must return empty output without reverting. Cryptographic library must be correctly implemented.

Gas cost must be calculated before execution using EIP-2565 formula: max(200, floor(complexity * iteration_count / 3)). Input lengths parsed from calldata must be validated. Minimum gas floor of 200 prevents spam.
Minimum gas floor of 200 must be enforced. Gas formula must accurately reflect actual computation cost across all client implementations to prevent underpricing attacks.

Full block structure validation required: header conformance to fork rules, state trie updates, bloom filter computation, and transaction execution. Invalid blocks must be rejected without state corruption.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Weak Subjectivity Checkpoint Validation (CLI startup parameter)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Checkpoint format must be parsed and validated: block root must match canonical chain at specified epoch. If checkpoint epoch > finalized epoch, block must exist in canonical chain. If checkpoint epoch <= finalized epoch, root must match. Invalid checkpoints must cause client termination with descriptive error.

Conflicting finalized checkpoints require at least 1/3 of total stake to be slashable. WS checkpoint must reject attacker forks. Safety margin of at least 1/3 - SAFETY_DECAY/100 (~23.3%) must be maintained within the WS period.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: PeerDAS Data Column Sidecar Gossip Verification
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Each data column sidecar must pass: (1) batched KZG commitment verification, (2) inclusion proof verification. Invalid columns must be rejected and validation failures tracked via metrics. Reconstruction of missing columns must only use verified data.
